data.body:
J3/J4 PLAN GATES.
J4 0a94 -> PASS first time (0 blocking, 1 generic P6 advisory). CLAIMED.
 BUT the reviewer MISSED a real defect that I found by reading the tree: AC4 says grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/ must return nothing, on the premise (true of PR #120, FALSE of this tree) that nothing sets that attribute. In rebar it IS set at outbound_field_diff.py:197-203 and read at backend.py:122. Satisfying the AC literally would mean widening the BACKEND-NEUTRAL port signature in _backend.py:130 (affecting every backend) plus renaming an unrelated local function at outbound_differ.py:500 — far outside J4's declared 3-file scope and exactly the core-risking change this epic sequenced away from. Rather than quietly doing something narrower I recorded the precise satisfiable reading on the ticket (identity models take the resolver as an EXPLICIT parameter, zero getattr discovery, so PR #120's unreachable-branch defect is unwritable; the anti-churn oracle stays as the teeth) and FILED THE REMAINDER as task 65d7-8270-bdc6-41f6 (impious-safe-bettong), linked discovered_from 0a94, with file_impact set. Did NOT edit J4's description, because that would stale the fresh attestation and refuse the claim — the lesson the previous session recorded.

J3 aac8 -> BLOCK #1 (3 blocking, 10 advisory). All three blockers verified by me in code before remediating:
 B1+B2 (E6/F1, G1G2, impact 1.0): AC3's grep '_load_adf|fit_text_to_adf_limit' could not prove 'reached only from inside AdfCodec' — it also matches the DEFINITIONS — and worse it can NEVER come back clean, because _load_adf is defined at outbound_fields.py:71 and used at 217 and 567-568, inside a LOCATION-PINNED file that is not a J3 edit target. The AC was unsatisfiable as written.
 B3 (G6, impact 1.0): genuine design ambiguity. Cloud has TWO rich-text paths with DIFFERENT behavior — backend.py:_fit_description composes normalize_description(fit_text_to_adf_limit(v)), while the sanitizer J2 landed is injected with the FIT STEP ONLY. A two-operation Protocol cannot express that, so whichever caller got re-pointed would silently change behavior and break J1's pins.
 REMEDIATION (full rewrite, 6.4k -> 11.4k chars):
  * Protocol widened to FOUR operations (fit_outbound / normalize_outbound / to_wire / decode_inbound) with a table of both implementations, so each existing caller composes exactly what it composes today. Recorded WHY two is insufficient. Also resolved that fit_text_to_adf_limit returns TEXT, not an ADF document — the wire conversion is a separate step (acli.py wraps with text_to_adf at the transport), which is why to_wire is its own operation.
  * AdfCodec PINNED TO THE CLOUD SIDE (adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py), not jira_family/. This was only an advisory but it is critical: putting it in jira_family/ would import the pinned adf.py and FAIL the very import-contract test J2 just landed.
  * Specified WikiTextCodec's previously-unstated limit (32767, matching the documented Jira text-field cap this codebase already uses for comments) and truncation marker (reusing adf._ADF_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX's wording), both as sourced named constants.
  * Replaced the broken grep with an enforced ALLOWLIST naming the four legitimate hit sites, plus zero hits under jira_family/ or jira_datacenter/.
  * Declared the inbound path and outbound_fields.py explicitly OUT OF SCOPE so the ACs match what the story actually delivers; added a back-out path and an expand-then-contract note.
J3 REVIEW #2 -> BLOCK, 3 blockers -> 1, 10 advisories -> 1. Remaining blocker (E6/F1): AC5 'exactly one definition of map_fields_to_remote exists in the tree' stated an invariant with NO proving mechanism. Verified the subtlety myself: there are TWO defs today and they are NOT duplicates — _backend.py:117 is the neutral Protocol declaration (ellipsis stub, must REMAIN) and adapters/jira/backend.py:59 is the concrete implementation. Rewrote AC5 to require an AST test that counts only defs with a REAL body, asserts exactly one, and asserts it lives under jira_family/. Review #3 running.
